scope: All 19 AI-applied and verified attached records in the exact 27-record workflow

results.reason: Prospective club surveillance reports lower-limb tendinopathy outcomes for a separable elite youth futsal subgroup, with published incidence results per 1,000 exposure hours.

Although soccer is separately reported, the injury counts come from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System emergency-department database, not prospective surveillance reported from participating football teams or their clinical staff.

The separable Olympic soccer results concern external medical-facility visits and use organising-committee, EMR and treating-hospital records, rather than prospective team/competition injury surveillance. Athlete headcounts do not supply an eligible exposure denominator.
The PDF is explicitly a letter to the editor, which the full-text criteria exclude regardless of the paper's references to football.

Soccer and futsal participants are pooled with handball, basketball and rugby athletes, without a separable football outcome. The study also obtains past-12-month injury histories and reports no eligible exposure denominator.
The supplied file is a Clin J Sport Med abstracts/proceedings PDF and the record is a conference abstract, not a usable full report.

This paper explicitly declares itself a systematic review and meta-analysis of injury epidemiology in elite and amateur soccer referees, includes 17 relevant studies, and can surface extraction-relevant primary surveillance studies.
A prospective five-season cohort of Turkish Super League football players used club medical surveillance and publishes training, match and combined injury rates per 1,000 hours.
The supplied file is a conference abstracts compilation and this record is a single abstract (NR. 60), not a usable full report.

The randomised in-season study prospectively monitored actual hamstring injuries in elite academy footballers, using team medical surveillance and GPS-quantified training and match exposure with direct group exposure totals.
The separable soccer findings come from a cross-sectional motor-function and health-history assessment, not prospective or repeated injury surveillance. It reports no eligible exposure denominator.

The study explicitly concerns recreational sports activities. Its additional use of publicly available secondary data and injury counts without an eligible exposure denominator further confirms ineligibility.
This prospective cohort follows adolescent male soccer players across 20 regional-league matches, uses physiotherapist injury surveillance, and reports an actual match-exposure incidence rate.

This is a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected middle-school surveillance: athletic trainers were embedded at events, collected injury and athlete-exposure data, and report separable soccer concussion rates per 1,000 athlete-exposures.

The statewide, season-long surveillance contains separable high-school soccer concussion findings and a mappable clinical definition, but it calculates incidence only from athletic participant counts per 100 player-seasons. It reports no time exposure, athlete-exposures, match-exposures, valid published time rate, or defensible derivation inputs.

This two-page BJSM PhD Academy Award item is an editorial-style thesis summary, not a report of one primary study or a declared eligible systematic review. It describes a thesis and cites the underlying articles rather than supplying a study-specific methods-and-results report for extraction.

Despite the word 'football' in the title, the cohort is NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision American football. The paper's comparison with soccer occurs only in the Introduction and does not supply a separable association-football dataset.

The source is the Danish National Patient Registry, supplemented by a retrospective questionnaire of registered patients and population/athlete registry figures. It does not report prospectively collected injury outcomes from current participating football teams or their clinical staff. Its sport-specific metric is per 100,000 registered athletes, not an eligible exposure denominator.

This two-page BJSM PhD Academy Award item summarises four thesis articles, including an underlying trial and secondary analysis, rather than reporting a single study's full methods and results. It is neither the underlying primary paper nor a declared eligible systematic/scoping/umbrella review or meta-analysis in its own right.
